# Dataset: `campus_90day_dataset.csv`

**Owner:** Member 2 (Developer 1 — Telemetry & Machine Learning)
**Generated by:** `src/pipelines/periodic_retraining/generate_synthetic_dataset.py`
**Rows:** 4,320 (90 days x 48 half-hour intervals)

## Why synthetic, not Building Data Genome 2 (BDG2)

The team guide recommends BDG2 as the real-world source. This development
environment has no outbound internet access — both `pip install <package>` and
`curl` to external hosts time out here — so BDG2 could not be downloaded.
Synthetic generation with documented assumptions is the guide's explicitly
allowed fallback ("If you generate it instead, that is acceptable — but write
your assumptions down"). If a machine with internet access becomes available,
re-point `ModelTrainer.data_path` at a converted BDG2 extract instead; no other
code changes are required since the trainer only depends on the CSV column
contract below.

## Column contract

Identical to the `meter_history` table in `backend/data/init.sql`, so this file
can be loaded directly into Postgres via `PostgresMeterHistoryRepository` for
integration testing:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `reading_date` | ISO date, 2026-06-01 through 2026-08-29 |
| `time_slot` | `HH:MM`, 48 per day |
| `base_load_kw` | Synthetic campus electrical demand |
| `solar_gen_kw` | Synthetic rooftop PV generation |
| `outdoor_temp_c` | Synthetic ambient temperature |
| `grid_tariff_lkr_kwh` | PUCSL-style time-of-use tariff band |
| `zone_occupancy_count` | Synthetic scheduled/estimated occupant count |

## Generative assumptions (all in `generate_synthetic_dataset.py`)

- **Deterministic seed** (`DEFAULT_SEED = 20260101`) — re-running the script
  reproduces byte-identical output; this is a reproducibility choice, not a
  claim that campus load is actually this repeatable.
- **Diurnal temperature curve**: a sinusoid peaking ~14:00 (~33.8°C) and
  troughing ~04:30 (~25.2°C), typical of Malabe, Sri Lanka's climate, plus:
  - a slow ±1.5°C sinusoidal drift across the 90-day window (an inter-monsoon
    lull moving toward a hotter dry spell), and
  - independent `±0.6°C` per-interval noise.
- **Occupancy**: weekday daytime (08:00–17:00) base of 220 occupants, dipping
  to 90 at the 12:00 lunch slot; near-empty at night and on weekends (Sat/Sun
  by `date.weekday()`); ±15 occupant noise per interval; a random ~5% of days
  are flagged as "event days" (e.g. convocation, open day) adding +300
  occupants between 09:00–15:00, so the anomaly detector has genuine spikes to
  catch.
- **Demand model**: `base_load_kw = 180 (night floor) + 300 (weekday daytime
  block, 08:00–17:00) + 12·max(0, temp − 27°C) (cooling load) + 0.08·occupancy
  (equipment/device load) + N(0, 8) noise`. The cooling and occupancy
  coefficients intentionally match the statistical fallback formula in
  `src/agents/telemetry/forecaster.py`, so the trained model is learning a
  noisier, more realistic version of the same underlying physics rather than
  an unrelated data-generating process — this keeps the RMSE/MAE comparison
  in `train_forecaster.py` meaningful rather than an artifact of mismatched
  assumptions.
- **Solar model**: a daylight-hours (06:00–18:00) half-sine profile peaking at
  ~210 kW, scaled per-day by a "clear sky factor" — 15% of days are randomly
  flagged overcast (0.35–0.6x yield), the rest are 0.85–1.05x, plus small
  per-interval noise.
- **Tariff bands**: 18:00–23:00 = LKR 58.00/kWh (peak), before 06:00 = LKR
  15.00/kWh (off-peak), else LKR 30.00/kWh (day) — matches the placeholder
  bands already used by `InMemoryMeterHistoryRepository`'s synthetic fallback.

## Known limitations (say this in the report)

- No real weather station or smart-meter data underlies any of the above —
  every number is a formula, not an observation.
- Only one "campus" is modeled; there is no cross-building or cross-campus
  variation.
- The demand and solar formulas are intentionally simple (linear/sinusoidal)
  so a linear-regression fallback model (see `train_forecaster.py`) can fit
  them reasonably well without needing LightGBM. A real campus's load is
  almost certainly less linear than this.
